properties.areaDesc: Indian River, FL; Okeechobee, FL
properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 21 at 6:19PM EST until November 21 at 6:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
SVRMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southwestern Indian River County in east central Florida...
Northeastern Okeechobee County in east central Florida...

* Until 645 PM EST.

* At 619 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm was located 6 miles northeast
of Basinger, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Fort Drum.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

properties.areaDesc: Lake Okeechobee
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 21 at 6:16PM EST until November 21 at 7:15PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Lake Okeechobee...

* Until 715 PM EST.

* At 616 PM EST, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from near Liberty
Point to 6 nm southwest of Clewiston, moving east at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Canal Point, Liberty Point, Sand Cut, Pahokee, Clewiston, Buckhead
Ridge, Lake Harbor, Calusa, and Moore Haven.
properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 21 at 3:15PM PST until November 23 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, south winds 15 to 25 kt
with gusts to 30 kt and seas 8 to 13 feet. For the Gale Watch,
southeast winds 20 to 30 kt with localized gusts to 50 kt and
seas 9 to 14 feet possible.

* WHERE...Coastal waters from Pt. St. George to Cape Mendocino
CA out 10 nm.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 3 AM PST Monday.
For the Gale Watch, from Monday afternoon through Tuesday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds can cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should consider altering plans to avoid possible
hazardous conditions.  Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter
course, and/or secure the vessel for severe wind and seas.

properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued November 21 at 6:07PM EST until November 21 at 6:30PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
At 606 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located over Kings Point, or near Boca Raton, moving northeast at
25 mph.

HAZARD...TORNADO.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Expect damage to mobile homes, roofs, and vehicles. Tree
damage is likely.

Locations impacted include...
Boca Raton, Boynton Beach, Delray Beach, Highland Beach, Ocean Ridge,
Lantana, Hamptons At Boca Raton, Village Of Golf, Kings Point, Dunes
Road, Whisper Walk, Hypoluxo, South Palm Beach, Gulf Stream, Briny
Breezes, Manalapan, Boca West, Morikami Park, Villages Of Oriole, and
Boca Raton Equestrian.
properties.instruction:
TAKE COVER NOW! Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile
home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and
protect yourself from flying debris.

NM...

located near Highland Beach, moving north at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 21 at 12:54PM PST until November 26 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA

flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4
AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST
Tuesday through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase
next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be
Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides
each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2
feet, likely re-breaking the all time tidal records set back in
late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain
around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell
Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf
beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf
heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10
feet on west-facing beaches.

NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical
predictions based on trends in recent observations.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 4:23PM AST until November 22 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo.

* WHEN...Through 6 AM AST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible. Most susceptible time of flooding will be
around the time of the morning high tides between about 730 AM
and 930 AM.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3
AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. Elevated to high surf is
expected much of the week, with even the possibility of warning-
level surf at times from Wednesday afternoon into Thursday.
Additional products will likely be needed into Friday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 21 at 2:02PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin, in combination
with strong north-northeast flow, has caused river levels on The St
Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises
through Major Flood Stage are forecast through the middle of next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Astronomical Tide or HAT.

The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS
EVENING TO 10 AM EST SUNDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 2:45AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert on Saturday for the
Susquehanna Valley.

A Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for
sensitive groups. Sensitive groups include children, people
suffering from asthma, heart disease or other lung diseases,
and the elderly. The effects of air pollution can be minimized
by avoiding strenuous activity or exercise outdoors.

For more information on ground-level ozone and fine particles,
visit www.airnow.gov, and www.aqpartners.state.pa.us.

properties.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in
effect from 6 PM Saturday November 21st to 10 AM EST Sunday November
22nd.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/
